document.instructions:
Onboarding proposal for a minimal Python service.

Discovered facts (verified by bounded reads): source root 'src' (src/app.py defines VALUE = 1); test root 'tests' (tests/test_app.py contains a unittest suite importing src.app); documentation root 'README.md'; dependency lock 'requirements.lock' (pip_requirements, sha256 29a659d071f1d7d73e4426e1fe451e0435379bc593ee1b6ed78de15a89aa35fe, no third-party dependencies); acceptance command candidate 'python -m unittest discover -s tests -v' from README.md line 3. No existing repository contract (canonical or alias) is present, so there is no alias conflict.

Proposed configuration: environment_profile 'python-3.11' copied exactly from contract_constraints.compatible_environment_profiles; its accepted_dependency_lock_kinds includes pip_requirements, matching the proposed dependency_lock. agent_network is denied and package_installation is preparation_only, consistent with the profile's python_hashed_requirements preparation strategy and denied lifecycle scripts.

Scope of THIS onboarding Run: only the controller-allowed configuration paths .pharness/repository.yaml, .pharness/instructions.md and .pharness/project.yaml may be written; no source, test, documentation or lock files are modified by this Run.

Proposed FUTURE development scope (candidate_contract.writable_paths): 'src/**' and 'tests/**' grant recursive descendant writes under the discovered source and test roots; 'README.md' grants that exact documentation file only. These derive solely from discovered source/test/documentation roots; they do not include the onboarding-only .pharness paths and do not authorize any edits during this onboarding Run. requirements.lock is intentionally outside the future writable scope because dependency_lock_generation is disabled and the lock is pinned by content hash.

Services: requested_service_keys is empty, so no binding change is proposed and no new Product Service is created; the existing 'finance-web' Service is neither rebound nor duplicated.

document.instructions:
Discovery summary (verified facts): Python repository at commit 2d61b80cc3db6949f9fa6ccbdb61afd49bd20596 with tracked paths .gitignore, README.md, pyproject.toml, src/app.py, tests/test_app.py. Root candidates src/ and tests/; documentation README.md; one command candidate 'python -m unittest discover -s tests -v' from README.md line 3 (untrusted prose, not adopted); one dependency candidate pyproject.toml of kind python_project; repository contract status missing with no alias; no discovery blockers, conflicts, submodules, or symlinks.

Decision: candidate_contract is null. Two independent defects prevent any truthful executable contract. (1) immutable_dependency_lock_missing: no pip_requirements or npm_package_lock file exists, the sole dependency candidate pyproject.toml is a mutable_dependency_input, and policy (dependency_lock_generation=false, network=denied) forbids generating a lock in this Run. (2) environment_profile_incompatible: contract_constraints.compatible_environment_profiles is empty, so no profile id can be copied into candidate_contract.environment_profile. Per the onboarding contract rule, missing executable facts must never be invented, so no roots, commands, lock, hash, or profile are proposed.

Scope distinction: this onboarding Run's allowed_source_changes are exactly .pharness/repository.yaml, .pharness/instructions.md, and .pharness/project.yaml. Because the proposal is blocked, no candidate_contract.writable_paths for future development are proposed, and this submission authorizes no source changes; a blocked proposal is retained evidence only. Had a contract been possible, future writable paths would have been derived from discovered roots (src/**, tests/**, README.md) and would have excluded the onboarding-only .pharness paths.

Services: requested_service_keys is empty, so no existing Service was requested for reuse; the existing Product Service finance-web (svc_finance_web) is not bound, and no new Services are proposed (empty service_proposals and binding_proposals).

Path to readiness: provide an immutable dependency lock at a tracked path (a pinned pip_requirements file or npm package-lock.json) with a known sha256, and make at least one compatible environment profile descriptor available whose accepted_dependency_lock_kinds matches that lock kind. On re-discovery with those facts, likely roots are source=src, tests=tests, documentation=README.md, with the README.md unittest discover command as an acceptance candidate subject to verification.
